title: The Late train on Monday
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：late　|　正文 333 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 late 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1990 the teacher wrote of ① a late train on Monday in the notebook, and everybody in the classroom said at once that it was ② later than the one named there the year before. Three terms on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the teacher, who never explained anything, had done it before dawn and gone home; it was the late ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the latest train on Monday anybody in the classroom had ever seen, or so the notebook for March 1984 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too late to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the pupil who had come to help; the late ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the ruler at the far blackboard, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a late work of the painter, and said that no pupil in his right mind would call it ⑥ as late as the work of the painter they had once had in the old classroom. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was late or not, and he said so.

By 1997 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the notebook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something late, and nothing besides. The pupil from the next classroom called the whole plan ⑧ quite late; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the notebook kept the names of the late ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 2000, in public, she wrote of another late train on Monday in the same notebook, and the work, which took two terms, seemed ⑨ later than anybody had expected. ⑩ The latest work of the painter in the whole classroom, she said in 2002, was the one she could never quite name; the late ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 迟（前置定语 a late train on Monday：1990 年先生在笔记簿里记下的那件迟的火车）
B. adj. 迟／晚年（比较级 later than：文中两处，一处比周一晚点的火车，一处比预想）
C. adj. 迟／晚年（最高级 the latest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 迟（表语 too late to do：母亲觉得它太迟，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 晚年（前置定语 a late work of the painter：叔叔把整件事称作一桩晚年的作品）
F. adj. 晚年（同级比较 as late as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩画家晚年的作品相比）
G. adj. 晚年（后置定语 something late：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 晚年（受程度副词修饰 quite late：那位学童的评价）

items.q: the latest train on Monday anybody
a late work of the painter
The latest work of the painter in

answers.why: late 意为“迟”，1990 年先生在笔记簿里记下的是“一件迟的火车”，此处作前置定语 a late train on Monday。
late 意为“迟”，此处用比较级 later than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
late 意为“迟”，笔记簿上 三月 那行字说它是教室里最迟的一件，故用最高级 the latest train on Monday。
late 意为“迟”，母亲认为这件东西“太迟了，谁也用不上”，too late to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
late 意为“晚年”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩晚年的作品”，此处作前置定语 a late work of the painter。
late 意为“晚年”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩画家晚年的作品一样晚年”，同级比较用 as late as。
late 意为“晚年”，笔记簿上那半行字要的是“晚年的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something late。
late 意为“晚年”，邻教室来的那位学童认为这套计划“相当晚年”，quite 修饰原级 late。
late 意为“晚年”，2000 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要晚年”，故用比较级 later than。
late 意为“晚年”，母亲 2002 年说的是“整个教室里最晚年的那一桩”，故用最高级 the latest work of the painter。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1990 年，先生在笔记簿里记下了一件迟的火车。（a late train on Monday）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更迟。（later than …）
母亲觉得它太迟，谁也用不上。（too late to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩晚年的作品。（a late work of the painter）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩画家晚年的作品一样晚年。（as late as …）
到了 1997 年，笔记簿上只剩半行字：要的是一件晚年的东西。（something late）
answers: In 1990 the teacher wrote of a late train on Monday in the notebook.
Everybody said it was later than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too late to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a late work of the painter.
He said nobody would call it as late as the work of the painter they had once had.
By 1997 the notebook asked for nothing but something late.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 late 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1990 the teacher wrote of a late train on Monday in the notebook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the latest train on Monday in the classroom, or so the notebook says.
My mother thought it too late to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a late work of the painter, and nobody argued with him.
The pupil from the next classroom called the plan quite late, and everybody laughed.
The late ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
